## Why build it this way

The aim is a site where each claim of a skill comes with evidence that can be checked, a date that can be verified, and an honest account of what generative artificial intelligence (AI) did.

Six decisions follow from that:

1. **Plain text in git.** Every entry is a text file in a public repository, so its full revision history is open, and each entry shows what changed from one version to the next.
2. **Checks before publishing.** A script scans every change for NHS numbers and similar identifiers, and blocks data files, before anything is committed.
3. **A required statement of AI use.** Every evidence entry has to say what generative AI did and what was done and checked by hand; projects still in progress add it when they are released. The build fails if it is missing.
4. **Nothing is published without review, with one exception.** Every change is checked and built automatically, but the site only goes live when publishing is started by hand. The exception is work logs: they publish themselves each night, and only when nothing else has changed since the last reviewed version.
5. **Projects stay private until finished; their timeline does not.** While a project's repository is private, the site shows only when work was done: each commit's fingerprint, time and size, nothing of its content or topic. When the project is finished, a clean copy is released, and its contents are checked against the private history.
6. **Reflections are fingerprinted when written.** Reflections written alongside the work stay private, and only a fingerprint of each is published that night. At release the texts appear and are checked against those fingerprints; any later edit is shown as such, with the original beside it.

## What was built

- A [Quarto](https://quarto.org) website with separate Evidence and Essays listings.
- A filter that adds the AI-use box, the evidence links, the work-log panel and a revision-history link to each entry.
- Header validation and a patient-data scan, run before each commit and again during the online build.
- An automatic build on every push, with publishing to GitHub Pages started by hand (work logs excepted).
- A nightly job in each private project that exports its work log and reflection fingerprints to this site.
- Checks that a published fingerprint is never dropped or changed, and that every released reflection's label ("matches" or "revised") is correct.
- A word-by-word comparison of every version of each entry, built from its git history.
